A VPN (virtual private network) is a service that sends your internet traffic through a protected, scrambled link to another computer before it reaches the websites you visit. Think of it as a private tunnel between your device and the wider internet.

Websites then see the location of that other computer instead of yours, and anyone on the same network, like café or airport Wi-Fi, can't read what you send. This helps with privacy on public networks, with reaching your office systems from home, and with using a service that is limited by region.

A VPN is not complete protection. The VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust. It also won't stop viruses or scams, and it can slow your connection a little.

VPN (virtual private network) ek private raasta hai jo aapke internet ko surakshit, scrambled link se doosre computer tak le jaata hai, aur phir wahan se websites tak. Ise aap ek private tunnel samajh sakte hain.

Websites ko aapki asli jagah nahi, us doosre computer ki jagah dikhti hai. Café ya airport ke Wi-Fi par bhi koi aapka data padh nahi sakta. Isse public Wi-Fi par privacy milti hai, ghar se office ka kaam ho paata hai, aur region ke hisaab se band services khul jaati hain.

VPN poori suraksha nahi hai. VPN company aapka internet use dekh sakti hai, isliye bharosemand wala chuniye. Yeh viruses ya scams nahi rokta, aur connection thoda slow ho sakta hai.
